title: Dedicated autoscaler: enforce priority SLOs in burst controls and improve utilization reporting
author: Alicia Chen
description: Motivation: customers running Dedicated fleets saw tail latency regressions when burst capacity kicked in for lower-priority workloads; autoscaler was allowing bursts that violated configured priority SLOs and reporting did not attribute burst usage correctly. This PR enforces priority-level SLO checks in the burst token bucket, introduces a priority-aware burst admission policy, and expands utilization reporting to surface per-priority burst consumption and SLO violations. Changes include controller logic, metrics/reporting, tests, docs, and a small Helm config update. Checklist: [x] Add priority SLO enforcement in autoscaler token bucket admission; [x] Adjust fallback decision to prefer high-priority pools when bursts would violate SLOs; [x] Emit new metrics (dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst_consumed, dedicated.autoscaler.slo_violations) and tag by priority and region; [x] Add integration tests that simulate multi-priority traffic and bursts; [x] Update docs and Helm values; [x] Run perf and canary on staging; Rollout plan: deploy to staging with feature-flag enabled for 48h, monitor slo_violations and latency p99; then ramp to low-traffic fleets before wide rollout. Impact: should reduce observed SLO breaches during bursts and give operators more visibility into which priorities consume burst tokens.
